description: AI Stack monitoring dashboard for the llama.cpp inference server, its AMD GPUs (currently 2× Radeon AI PRO R9700; pick cards with the GPU variable), and the host system. Covers GPU VRAM/compute/thermals, LLM token throughput, MoE RAM offloading, CPU, storage, and system health.

panels.description:
VRAM allocated vs. free, one line per GPU (32 GB each on the Radeon AI PRO R9700s).

Key signals:
• GPU n Used GB — climbing toward 31-32GB on a card risks OOM (orange/red thresholds at 30/31.5GB).
• GPU n Free GB — should track inversely with Used; a sudden jump up means a model crashed or was unloaded.
• GPU n Total GB (reference) — flat at ~32GB, just a scale anchor.
• With a model split across both cards, expect Used to rise on both GPUs together.
panels.title: VRAM Usage

panels.description:
Shader/compute vs. memory-controller utilization, one line per GPU.

Key signals:
• Compute (gfx) % — high value means the GPU core is compute-bound (matrix multiply saturated).
• Memory Controller (umc) % — high value means VRAM bandwidth-bound; usually the dominant bottleneck for MoE models since experts stream from memory.
• gfx high + umc low = compute-bound; umc high = bandwidth-bound (expected for large MoE models).
• With a model split across both cards (layer split), the GPUs take turns being busy rather than peaking together.
panels.title: GPU Compute & Memory Activity

panels.description:
Power draw per GPU against its configured cap.

Key signals:
• GPU n Instantaneous (W) — spiky moment-to-moment draw.
• GPU n Average Package (W) — smoothed reading, easier to read the trend.
• Power Cap PCI xx:xx (W) — each card's ceiling (R9700: 300W board power; check with rocm-smi); if Instantaneous rides the cap continuously, that GPU is power-limited.
panels.title: GPU Power

panels.description:
Die, hotspot, and memory temperatures, one line per GPU.

Key signals:
• Edge °C — die surface, generally the lowest reading.
• Junction/Hotspot °C — hottest point on the die; throttling begins ~110°C, emergency shutdown ~115°C; keep below 95°C under sustained load.
• Memory °C — GDDR6 temp; above 95°C memory clocks reduce, directly hurting throughput since VRAM bandwidth is the primary inference bottleneck.
• Two cards side by side: the upper card usually runs hotter since it breathes the lower card's exhaust.
panels.title: GPU Temperatures

panels.description:
PCIe traffic between each GPU and the rest of the system.

Key signals:
• GPU n PCIe Bandwidth (Mb/s) — the data highway for MoE expert weight fetches (-ot CPU-offload) and, with a model split across both cards, for activations passed between them; expected to spike during inference. Both R9700s link at PCIe 5.0 x16 (~63 GB/s); pegged near that ceiling means PCIe bandwidth, not compute, is the bottleneck — consider offloading fewer experts.
panels.title: PCIe Bandwidth (MoE Expert Transfer)

panels.description:
System RAM each GPU has DMA-mapped (GTT) for CPU-offloaded MoE expert weights.

Key signals:
• GPU n GTT Used GB — expect 10-15GB when a model with -ot CPU-offloaded experts is loaded; near-zero while a model runs means experts landed in regular malloc RAM instead (still works, may be slightly slower).
• GPU n GTT Free GB — headroom against the GTT pool.

targets.legendFormat: GPU {{gpu_id}} GTT Used GB (MoE experts in RAM)

panels.title: GTT Memory (System RAM Mapped for GPU)

panels.description:
Requests actively generating vs. waiting, per model.

Key signals:
• {{model}} processing — normally 0 or 1 in single-user use.
• {{model}} deferred (queued) — requests waiting because the server is busy; growth here means concurrent requests are being sent (e.g. multiple clients hitting the router), which should be rare for personal use.
panels.title: Request Queue

panels.description:
Prefill-phase tokens/sec — digesting the input prompt before generation starts.

Key signals:
• {{model}} tokens/sec — usually much faster than decode (100-500 tok/s). A slow prefill points to a very large context or KV-cache pressure; large file maps in agentic/architect workflows can take several seconds here.
panels.title: Prompt Processing Speed (prefill phase)

panels.description:
Decode-phase tokens/sec — what you experience as typing speed.

Key signals:
• {{model}} tokens/sec — per active router model (Baloza-v0.3, ninni-v0.1). Typical range 15-40 tok/s; a sustained drop signals GPU thermal throttling, VRAM pressure, PCIe saturation from MoE fetches, or RAM exhaustion causing swap.
panels.title: Token Generation Speed (decode phase)

panels.description:
Smoothed generation throughput over a trailing 5-minute window.

Key signals:
• {{model}} avg tok/s (5m) — a less noisy view of decode speed than the instantaneous panel; use it to spot gradual degradation (thermal throttling, memory pressure) that a single spiky reading would hide.
panels.title: Average Token Throughput (5m rate)

panels.description:
Host memory availability — critical because MoE experts live in RAM/GTT, not just VRAM.

Key signals:
• Available GB — free + reclaimable page cache; must stay above ~8GB or the kernel starts evicting MoE expert pages, forcing re-reads from disk and cratering inference speed.
• Used GB — climbing steadily alongside Available dropping is the early warning sign.
• Page Cache GB — includes model weight pages; shrinks under memory pressure as the kernel reclaims it.
panels.title: RAM Overview (64 GB total)

panels.description:
Any use of swap or its compressed front-end during inference is a red flag.

Key signals:
• Swap Used GB — must stay at 0 during inference; any activity means MoE expert weights are being paged to disk, which can tank generation speed from ~30 tok/s to <1 tok/s.
• Zswap Compressed GB — a compressed RAM cache in front of swap; better than disk swap but still indicates memory pressure building.
• Swap Cached GB — pages that were swapped out and read back in without being modified.
panels.title: Swap & Zswap (must be 0 during inference)

panels.description:
Fraction of time processes were stalled waiting for memory or disk I/O.

Key signals:
• Memory Stalled — most sensitive MoE RAM-pressure indicator; above 0.1 during inference means the kernel can't serve expert weight pages fast enough.
• Memory Waiting — softer precursor to Stalled.
• I/O Stalled / I/O Waiting — should sit near 0; a spike means something is hitting disk (swap activity, log writes, Docker overlay writes).
panels.title: Pressure Stall Index — Memory & I/O (PSI)

panels.description:
Live swap-in/out rate — the signal that actually matters for inference degradation, unlike the static Swap Used gauge above.

Key signals:
• pswpout (swap-out) — nonzero for a sustained period means the kernel is actively paging things to disk right now, which is what actually hurts inference speed.
• pswpin (swap-in) — something previously swapped out just got touched and read back.
• Both flat at zero is normal even when Swap Used stays elevated — a static leftover footprint from a past memory-pressure event is harmless; only active churn here matters. Backs the 'Active swap-out churn' alert.
panels.title: Swap Activity (pages/sec)

panels.description:
Overall CPU load across all 32 threads during inference.

Key signals:
• CPU Utilization % — expect 10-40% during active inference even though the GPU does the matrix math; the CPU handles MoE expert dispatch, KV-cache management, tokenisation, and Docker/network overhead.
• iowait % — should be near 0; elevated iowait means a disk bottleneck (swap activity, model re-reads, Docker overlay writes).
• system % — kernel-space CPU time; sustained high values alongside iowait point to the same disk-bottleneck causes.
panels.title: CPU Utilization

panels.description:
Per-core clock speed — flags whether the powersave governor is limiting inference.

Key signals:
• Avg GHz — overall clock average.
• Min GHz (parked cores) — on the powersave governor idle cores park at ~624MHz, slowing MoE expert dispatch; switch to performance governor for inference workloads (echo performance | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor).
• Max GHz (boost) — should approach the ~5.7GHz boost ceiling under load on the performance governor.
panels.title: CPU Frequency

panels.description:
Zen 5 die and VRM temperatures (Tctl needs a known offset correction).

Key signals:
• Tctl (includes +27°C offset) — what most tools report; not the real die temp on Zen 5 (67°C here ≈ 40°C actual) — use Tccd for the real number.
• Tccd1/Tccd2 (die 1/2 actual) — real per-die temperatures (16 cores each).
• CPU Package (ASUS EC) — motherboard's overall package reading.
• VRM — voltage regulator temp; above 90°C causes CPU throttling.
panels.title: CPU Temperatures

panels.description:
Read/write throughput on sda, the system disk.

Key signals:
• Read/Write MB/s — should sit near-idle during normal inference; sustained activity suggests OS/Docker overlay writes, log growth, or swap spilling onto this disk.
panels.title: Storage Throughput — system (sda)

panels.description:
Read/write throughput on the NVMe drive backing /data, where models live.

Key signals:
• Read MB/s — a large burst here during model load is expected (reading a ~20GB model file off disk).
• Write MB/s — should be near-idle outside model downloads; sustained writes during inference are unexpected.
panels.title: Storage Throughput — NVMe /data Drive (nvme0n1)

panels.description:
Free space across the mounts that matter for model storage and the OS.

Key signals:
• /data free GB — model storage; colored by percentage remaining since each Q4_K_XL model download is roughly 20GB.
• / free GB — root filesystem; holds Docker images and system packages.
• /home free GB — user data.
panels.title: Filesystem Free Space

panels.description:
Runnable + uninterruptible process count, averaged over 1/5/15 minutes.

Key signals:
• 1m / 5m / 15m load — the system has 32 threads, so load of 32 means every thread is occupied; sustained load above 32 means processes are queuing for CPU time. Load of 4-8 during active inference (e.g. agentic coding workflows) is normal.
panels.title: Load Average (32 threads total)

panels.description:
RX/TX throughput on the active WiFi interface (wlan0; the br-* bridge serves Docker containers).

Key signals:
• WiFi RX MB/s — large receive spikes mean model downloads or Docker image pulls.
• WiFi TX MB/s — large transmit spikes mean a long generated response streaming out to a LAN client (phone, tablet, browser).
panels.title: Network Throughput (WiFi)

panels.description:
NVMe and motherboard thermals, plus GPU memory error-correction status.

Key signals:
• NVMe Temp °C — most NVMe drives throttle reads at 70-75°C, slowing model load times; keep below 65°C for sustained throughput.
• Motherboard °C — general board-level thermal reading.
• GPU ECC Uncorrectable Errors — must always be 0; any non-zero value indicates a hardware memory fault that could silently corrupt model weights and produce garbage output.
panels.title: NVMe Temp / Motherboard Temp / GPU ECC

panels.description:
Which router-mode model (of models.ini) is currently resident and serving.

Key signals:
• Green tile = that model is currently loaded (up=1).
• Red tile = not loaded (up=0) — expected for the inactive model under --models-max 1, not an error by itself.
• If both tiles are red, the router has no model loaded at all.
panels.title: Currently Loaded Model
